## Classes

### <a name="openvox_server"></a>`openvox_server`

Installs openvox-server from a collection, together with the openvox-agent
it requires, and keeps the service running. Assign it to the host that
runs your OpenVox Server; the agent on that host applies it against the
server it manages.

What a run does:

1. Installs the collection's release package in place of other OpenVox and
   Puppet major versions' release packages, and ensures openvox-agent at
   `agent_package_version`, through
   [openvox_agent](https://forge.puppet.com/modules/miharp/openvox_agent),
   which on its own leaves server hosts alone (`manage_agent`,
   `manage_repo`).
2. Ensures openvox-server at `package_version`, ordered between the
   repository and the agent: the server package requires an agent of its
   own major, so moving it across a major moves the agent in the same
   package transaction, and the agent's own pin is applied after. When
   openvox_agent leaves the host alone, because its agent would lose the
   implicit server that OpenVox 9 removed, the server stays where it is
   too.
3. Owns `webserver.conf`: the address and port the server listens on,
   whether it asks clients for a certificate, the access log configuration,
   and any further `webserver` settings given (`manage_webserver`).
4. Sets the `[server]` settings in `puppet.conf` and the renewal settings
   in `ca.conf` that are given, and leaves the rest of both files alone.
5. Keeps the CA service enabled in `services.d/ca.cfg`, and before the
   service ever starts, when no CA exists yet, runs `puppetserver ca setup`
   so the CA is a root plus a 15-year intermediate rather than the single
   self-signed certificate the service makes for itself on first start
   (`manage_ca`).
6. Applies the JVM heap, reserved code cache and JRuby instance count it
   is given, through [openvox_tune](https://forge.puppet.com/modules/miharp/openvox_tune),
   whose `openvox_tune::tune` plan recommends them for the host. On a host
   where the server is installed in the same run, they apply from the next
   run (`manage_tuning`).
7. Keeps the `puppetserver` service running and enabled. The service is
   restarted when the package, `webserver.conf`, `services.d/ca.cfg` or
   the JVM arguments change, and reloaded, which keeps the JVM and takes a
   few seconds, when `puppet.conf`, `ca.conf` or the JRuby instance count
   changes (`manage_service`). A reload falls back to a restart where the
   service cannot be reloaded.

Before that, it warns (and does nothing about it) when the host has less
memory than 1.1 times the server's heap, below which the server refuses to
start, and when the Java the installed server runs is not one it supports:
OpenVox Server 8 needs Java 17 or 21, OpenVox Server 9 needs 21 or 25.

A host running neither openvox-server nor openvox-agent, such as a Puppet 7
server, has no collection to default to and takes an explicit `collection`.
OpenVox Server 9 is not packaged for Debian 12, which lacks the Java 21 it
needs; a Debian 12 host stays on `openvox8`.

#### Examples

##### Standard install from the agent's collection

```puppet
include openvox_server
```

##### Move a server from OpenVox 8 to 9

```puppet
class { 'openvox_server':
  collection      => 'openvox9',
  package_version => 'latest',
}
```

##### Sized for an 8 CPU, 16 GB host, from the openvox_tune::tune plan

```puppet
class { 'openvox_server':
  max_active_instances   => 7,
  heap_mb                => 4096,
  reserved_code_cache_mb => 1024,
}
```

##### A CA with a name of its own, renewing agent certificates

```puppet
class { 'openvox_server':
  ca_name               => 'Example CA',
  dns_alt_names         => ['puppet', 'puppet.example.com'],
  allow_auto_renewal    => true,
  auto_renewal_cert_ttl => '90d',
}
```

##### <a name="-openvox_server--collection"></a>`collection`

Data type: `Optional[Pattern[/\Aopenvox\d+\z/]]`

The collection to install from, such as `openvox8` or `openvox9`. When
unset, the installed server stays on the collection of the version it
runs; on a host without a server, the collection of the OpenVox agent
applying the catalog is used. Moving between majors takes an explicit
collection.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-openvox_server--package_version"></a>`package_version`

Data type: `String[1]`

`present` (install if missing, never upgrade), `latest`, or a version such
as `9.0.1`. A bare version is expanded to the package version for the
platform (`9.0.1-1.el9`, `9.0.1-1+ubuntu24.04`); one containing a `-` is
used as it is.

Default value: `'present'`

##### <a name="-openvox_server--agent_package_version"></a>`agent_package_version`

Data type: `String[1]`

The same for openvox-agent on this host, passed to openvox_agent. The
agent must share the server's major version.

Default value: `'present'`

##### <a name="-openvox_server--manage_repo"></a>`manage_repo`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether openvox_agent installs the collection's release package and
removes other majors' release packages. Turn it off when the repository
comes from somewhere else, such as a mirror configured by another
module.

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-openvox_server--apt_source"></a>`apt_source`

Data type: `Pattern[/\Ahttps?:\/\/\S+[^\/]\z/]`

Base URL the Debian and Ubuntu release package is downloaded from.

Default value: `'https://apt.voxpupuli.org'`

##### <a name="-openvox_server--yum_source"></a>`yum_source`

Data type: `Pattern[/\Ahttps?:\/\/\S+[^\/]\z/]`

Base URL the EL release package is downloaded from.

Default value: `'https://yum.voxpupuli.org'`

##### <a name="-openvox_server--manage_agent"></a>`manage_agent`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether to declare the openvox_agent class, which manages the
repository and openvox-agent on this host. Turn it off when something
else does both; `manage_repo` then has no effect.

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-openvox_server--java_package"></a>`java_package`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

A JRE package to install before the server. Not needed with released
packages, which pull in a supported JRE; for pre-release testing where
the server needs a Java the package does not yet require.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-openvox_server--manage_webserver"></a>`manage_webserver`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether to own `webserver.conf`. Turn it off to manage the file some
other way; `ssl_host`, `ssl_port`, `client_auth`, `access_log_config`
and `webserver_extra_settings` then do nothing.

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-openvox_server--ssl_host"></a>`ssl_host`

Data type: `String[1]`

The address the server listens on, `webserver.ssl-host`.

Default value: `'0.0.0.0'`

##### <a name="-openvox_server--ssl_port"></a>`ssl_port`

Data type: `Integer[1, 65535]`

The port the server listens on, `webserver.ssl-port`.

Default value: `8140`

##### <a name="-openvox_server--client_auth"></a>`client_auth`

Data type: `Enum['want', 'need', 'none']`

`webserver.client-auth`: whether a connecting client is asked for a
certificate (`want`, the default), must present one (`need`), or is not
asked (`none`). Agents authenticate with their certificate, so `none`
only makes sense behind a proxy that does.

Default value: `'want'`

##### <a name="-openvox_server--access_log_config"></a>`access_log_config`

Data type: `Pattern[/\A\//]`

`webserver.access-log-config`, the logback configuration of the request
log; the package ships one.

Default value: `'/etc/puppetlabs/puppetserver/request-logging.xml'`

##### <a name="-openvox_server--webserver_extra_settings"></a>`webserver_extra_settings`

Data type: `Hash[String[1], Variant[String, Numeric, Boolean, Array[Variant[String, Numeric, Boolean]]]]`

Further `webserver` settings, by their HOCON name, such as
`idle-timeout-milliseconds` or `ssl-protocols`. Strings are quoted,
numbers and booleans are bare, arrays are lists. The settings the
parameters above own cannot be given here.

Default value: `{}`

##### <a name="-openvox_server--manage_tuning"></a>`manage_tuning`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether to apply `max_active_instances`, `heap_mb` and
`reserved_code_cache_mb` through the openvox_tune class. Turn it off to
declare that class yourself, or to size the server some other way.

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-openvox_server--max_active_instances"></a>`max_active_instances`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[1]]`

JRuby instances, `jruby-puppet.max-active-instances`, set in
`conf.d/openvox_tune.conf`. Unset, the file is removed and the server's
default applies.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-openvox_server--heap_mb"></a>`heap_mb`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[512]]`

JVM heap in MB, set as `-Xms` and `-Xmx` in `JAVA_ARGS`, keeping the
other arguments. Unset, left as it is.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-openvox_server--reserved_code_cache_mb"></a>`reserved_code_cache_mb`

Data type: `Optional[Integer[32]]`

JVM reserved code cache in MB, `-XX:ReservedCodeCacheSize` in
`JAVA_ARGS`. Unset, left as it is.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-openvox_server--manage_ca"></a>`manage_ca`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether to keep the CA service enabled in `services.d/ca.cfg` and to set
the CA up with `puppetserver ca setup` before the first start. An existing
CA is never touched.

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-openvox_server--ca_name"></a>`ca_name`

Data type: `Optional[Pattern[/\A[^'"]+\z/]]`

The common name of the intermediate signing certificate `puppetserver ca
setup` creates, in place of `Puppet CA: <certname>`. Only used when the
CA is created.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-openvox_server--subject_alt_names"></a>`subject_alt_names`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String[1]]]`

Subject alternative names for the server's own certificate when
`puppetserver ca setup` creates it. When unset, `dns_alt_names` applies.
Only used when the CA is created.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-openvox_server--allow_auto_renewal"></a>`allow_auto_renewal`

Data type: `Optional[Boolean]`

`certificate-authority.allow-auto-renewal` in `ca.conf`: whether the CA
renews agent certificates that ask. When unset, the file's value is left
as it is.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-openvox_server--auto_renewal_cert_ttl"></a>`auto_renewal_cert_ttl`

Data type: `Optional[Pattern[/\A\d+[smhdy]\z/]]`

`certificate-authority.auto-renewal-cert-ttl` in `ca.conf`, the lifetime
of renewed certificates, such as `60d`. When unset, left as it is.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-openvox_server--dns_alt_names"></a>`dns_alt_names`

Data type: `Optional[Array[String[1]]]`

`dns_alt_names` in the `[server]` section of `puppet.conf`: the names
the server's certificate is valid for when the server requests one. When
unset, left as it is.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-openvox_server--autosign"></a>`autosign`

Data type: `Optional[Variant[Boolean, Pattern[/\A\//]]]`

`autosign` in `[server]`: `true` to sign every request, `false` to sign
none, or the path of an autosign configuration file or script. When
unset, left as it is.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-openvox_server--ca_server"></a>`ca_server`

Data type: `Optional[String[1]]`

`ca_server` in `[server]`: the CA this server sends certificate requests
to, for a compiler. When unset, left as it is.

Default value: `undef`

##### <a name="-openvox_server--manage_service"></a>`manage_service`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether to manage the server service.

Default value: `true`

##### <a name="-openvox_server--service_name"></a>`service_name`

Data type: `String[1]`

The server service. The openvox-server package keeps the `puppetserver`
service name.

Default value: `'puppetserver'`

##### <a name="-openvox_server--service_ensure"></a>`service_ensure`

Data type: `Enum['running', 'stopped']`

Whether the service should be running.

Default value: `'running'`

##### <a name="-openvox_server--service_enable"></a>`service_enable`

Data type: `Boolean`

Whether the service starts at boot.

Default value: `true`
